faqs.q: When can bats be removed from a Yorktown attic?
faqs.a: Bats in Virginia are handled by exclusion only — one-way exits fitted and every other opening sealed so the colony leaves on its own. Under our permit conditions the maternity season runs May 1 through August 15, and bats may not be excluded or removed then unless no young are present or there is a threat to human health or safety, so we inspect any time but schedule most Yorktown exclusions outside that window. Since January 1, 2025, bat work also requires a CNAP holder with DWR-recognized bat training, which is how our crew works.

faqs.q: Why do Grafton squirrel quotes focus on the whole roofline instead of the one hole?
faqs.a: Because Grafton's subdivisions were built street by street with the same materials, and those materials are aging together. The hole above your bedroom is the one the squirrels are using today; the gable vent and the addition joint are the same age and the same softness. We quote the entries we find plus the weak points we can show you in photos, priced as one roofline job — it is nearly always cheaper than three separate call-outs as each remaining gap gets discovered by the next squirrel.

faqs.q: Rats are getting into Grafton garages from the corridor — how do you stop it for good?
faqs.a: By treating the garage like the food warehouse rats believe it is. Norway rats are a designated nuisance species in Virginia, and the work is trapping plus exclusion: door sweeps and sill gaps sealed, birdseed and pet food into metal containers, and the fence-line runs and brush that shelter travel routes cleared back. A Grafton block behind restaurants may need several homes sealed before the pressure drops — we will tell you honestly if your house alone is sealed tight and the problem is arriving faster than any one property can fix.

Grafton.wildlife_intro:
Grafton is where York County suburbanized — brick two-stories street after street along Route 17, with headwater branches of the Poquoson River threading wooded buffers between the subdivisions. That buffer pattern delivers gray squirrels to every roofline in the neighborhood at once: they travel the creek woods, enter at the weakest soffit on the street, and raise two litters a year in Grafton's big, warm attics. The corridor adds the commercial side — Norway rats behind the restaurants and dumpsters, working their way into garage and crawlspace runs in the streets behind.

Subdivision work here is pattern work. One squirrel family on a Grafton street usually means the whole street's same-age soffits are failing together, so we show homeowners the entry style their builder used and what its lifespan is — then seal with material that outlasts it. For the rat calls, the inspection extends to the garage and the fence line, because corridor rats treat a subdivision as a network, not an address.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to get a raccoon family out of a Tabb chimney?
faqs.a: Chimney families are priced as a full sequence: confirming the litter, removing mother and young together, cleaning the flue shelf, and fitting a proper cap before we leave — because an uncapped Tabb chimney beside the marsh will host another family next spring. The variables are flue size and condition, how deep the family is denned, and whether the soffits need sealing too. We inspect, photograph the flue, and quote the whole sequence in writing; the cap is never an upsell, it is the step that makes the removal permanent.

faqs.q: Is the snake in my Tabb ditch a cottonmouth?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not — and we understand why you ask. Tabb's ditches and marsh edges are full of northern watersnakes, heavy-bodied and dark, which are harmless fish-eaters and the region's great cottonmouth impersonators. True northern cottonmouths in Virginia are confined to the lower southeastern Coastal Plain — the Back Bay and Great Dismal Swamp country south and east of Petersburg — not York County. Send us a photo from a safe distance: if it is a watersnake, the right service is leaving it to its frogs. If a snake ever does need moving, a permit holder can move a non-listed snake a short distance within the same or a neighboring county, with the release-site landowner's written permission, reported to DWR.

Tabb.wildlife_intro:
Tabb sits on a narrow neck between two kinds of wet — Big Bethel Reservoir's woods on one side, the Poquoson River and Back River marshes on the other — and its subdivisions took the high ground in between. Raccoons are Tabb's headline animal: marsh and reservoir feed them year-round, and spring mothers den in the uncapped chimneys and soffit corners of the brick subdivisions, sometimes two streets deep from the water. Evening bats hunt the marsh edge at dusk and roost in the same older rooflines, and northern watersnakes in the drainage ditches give a scare a month to homeowners who mistake them for something venomous.

The Tabb pattern is proximity: no street here is far from water or woods, so sealing quality decides everything. We evict raccoon families at the structure — Virginia law does not allow moving them elsewhere — cap the flue the same visit, and walk the marsh-side fence lines for the ground-level gaps that let skunks and opossums into crawlspaces. A Tabb home sealed properly can sit between marsh and reservoir for years without a repeat call.

faqs.q: A snake turned up at my Seaford home — what happens next?
faqs.a: Call us and keep people and pets clear until we identify it. Most Seaford snake calls are harmless rat snakes, racers, or garter snakes, and the eastern copperhead — venomous and found statewide — is the one to treat with real caution. Snakes are the one class Virginia allows a permit holder to move a short distance: same or neighboring county or city, suitable habitat, with the release-site landowner's written permission, and we report the move to DWR. We never kill a snake as a marketed service.
